text: That works out to about one-sixteenth of the grown-ups per child that our brains evolved with (Perry, 2023). So the emptiness you feel (the "Void") is real, since it's what that missing company feels like. And once you've de-armored, going back to a lonely life will feel worse than it did with the armor on. I'd gather a tribe of people you're close to and see most days, because without them you'll eventually reach for the armor again just to survive the cold.
section: Psychology is the Software; Biology is the Hardware., after Perry's ratio of grown-ups to children
reader: an adult with trauma who has done years of therapy and still gets triggered, reading why the protocol starts with the body, who lives mostly alone
